documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

29 y/o woman here to establish care. Coming from another primary care office in the area; records release signed today.

HPI
1. Migraine. Has had migraines for years, no aura. Unilateral throbbing headache with nausea and light sensitivity, typically 2-3 a month, worse when she is short on sleep. Sumatriptan 50 mg works within an hour most times; rarely needs the second dose. No headaches on more than a few days a month. No new pattern, no neuro symptoms.
2. Opioid use disorder. Past IV heroin use. Entered an opioid treatment program in 2014 and has been on methadone since; current dose 60 mg daily, stable, observed dosing with take-homes. No illicit use since starting the program. No alcohol since entering treatment either. She is proud of this and wants it in her record accurately. Signed 42 CFR Part 2 consent so I can speak with the program's prescriber.

PMH: as above. No surgeries. No pregnancies.
Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP); sumatriptan 50 mg prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: Mother - hypothyroidism, postpartum depression. Father - migraines. Maternal aunt - bipolar I. Sister - Hashimoto's.
SH: Married. Admin assistant at the community college. Former smoker, quit early 2015. No alcohol. No current drug use.

ROS: negative except as above.

EXAM
Vitals reviewed. Well-appearing, pleasant.
HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged, no nodules.
Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.
Abdomen soft, nontender.
Skin: old track-mark scarring both antecubital fossae, no active lesions.
Neuro: CN II-XII intact, normal gait, fundi sharp.

ASSESSMENT / PLAN
1. Migraine without aura - well controlled. Continue sumatriptan 50 mg prn, max 200 mg/day; keep use under 10 days/month. Headache diary if frequency climbs.
2. OUD in sustained remission on methadone - continue with OTP. Naloxone nasal spray prescribed for home, husband shown how to use it (he is in the waiting room). Will coordinate with the program; requesting dose letter.
3. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hep C screening and hep B serologies given IV drug use history. She thinks her last Pap was last year and normal, will confirm with records. Flu shot when stock arrives in October.

RTC for physical in about a year, sooner prn.

Baby may need monitoring for neonatal withdrawal after birth; breastfeeding on methadone is encouraged. She had already talked with her counselor and is reassured.
- Sumatriptan: use sparingly once pregnant; acetaminophen first line. Data for sumatriptan in pregnancy are reasonably reassuring if she needs it occasionally.
- Folate: start prenatal vitamin with folic acid now.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 12/20/2018

CC: right lower quadrant pain x 8 hours

HPI: 32 y/o F on methadone maintenance for opioid use disorder in remission, history of migraine. Woke this morning with RLQ pain, sharp and constant, now 8 hours, worse with any movement and with the car ride in. No nausea or vomiting. Bowel habits unchanged. LMP about 3 weeks ago, normal. Actively trying to conceive.

Meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP - confirmed dose with program), prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: former smoker, no alcohol, no current drug use.

Exam: T 38.2 C (100.8 F), BP 130/85, HR 95, RR 18.
Uncomfortable, lying still. Abdomen: RLQ tenderness with rebound. No guarding, no rigidity. Pelvic exam: no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal fullness, no discharge.

Data: UA unremarkable. Urine hCG negative. WBC 12.0 K/uL, 80% neutrophils.
US: gallbladder, liver, kidneys normal. 3 cm fluid-filled structure in right adnexa with surrounding free fluid.

MDM: Fever, leukocytosis with left shift, RLQ peritoneal signs. Negative hCG makes ectopic unlikely. Differential appendicitis vs. adnexal process (ovarian cyst rupture, torsion). Exam favors appendicitis. Discussed with general surgery, who will take her for diagnostic laparoscopy.

Pain: IV acetaminophen; methadone continued, today's dose already taken at the program.
Disposition: admitted to general surgery.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets by mouth every 6 hours as needed for pain; max 6 tablets per day
Take 1 tablet by mouth every 6 hours with food as needed for pain, for up to 5 days

reports.text: Specimen: appendix. Gross: vermiform appendix with a congested, fibrin-coated serosa. Microscopic: transmural neutrophilic infiltrate with mucosal ulceration and serositis. No perforation identified. No dysplasia or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Acute appendicitis with periappendicitis. Negative for malignancy.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY (received by fax)
Admitted 12/20/2018 - Discharged 12/22/2018
Service: General Surgery

Diagnosis: acute appendicitis
Procedure: laparoscopic appendectomy 12/20/2018

Course: Taken to the OR the evening of admission. At laparoscopy the appendix was inflamed and distended and lay low in the pelvis against the right adnexa, with a small amount of cloudy free fluid around it, which accounts for the fluid-filled structure on ultrasound. Right ovary and tube looked normal; left adnexa normal. Appendix removed without difficulty, base healthy. Fluid suctioned and pelvis irrigated. No complications.

Post-op she had mild pain controlled with scheduled acetaminophen and ibuprofen; she preferred to avoid additional opioids and none were needed. Methadone 60 mg continued daily with confirmation from her program. Tolerating diet, ambulating, afebrile on discharge.

Pathology: acute appendicitis, no malignancy.

Discharge meds: methadone 60 mg daily (OTP, unchanged), acetaminophen 1000 mg q6h prn, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn x 5 days, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no lifting > 10 lb for 2 weeks; may shower. Surgical clinic in 2 weeks. See PCP within the week.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT NOTE (received from regional hospital)
Date of service: 11/26/2019

Chief complaint: behaving strangely, confused; 10 days postpartum.

History is mostly from her husband. Patient is 33, delivered her first baby 10 days ago (uncomplicated vaginal delivery). Since coming home she has barely slept. Over several days she has become increasingly odd - he hears her talking to herself and she seems to be answering voices he can't hear. Tonight she told him the baby is possessed and that she has to protect her from evil spirits, which is what brought them in. No known head injury, fever or substance use; she has had her methadone at the program daily. Seen in this ED last December for appendicitis.

PMH: migraine without aura; opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg daily; appendectomy 12/2018.

Allergies: NKDA.
FH: maternal aunt with bipolar I; mother with postpartum depression and hypothyroidism.
SH: married, former smoker (quit 2015), no alcohol since entering treatment, works as administrative assistant at a community college.

Exam: vital signs within normal limits. Agitated, distracted, appears to be attending to internal stimuli. Oriented to person only - not to place or date. No focal neurologic deficit. Abdomen soft, fundus firm below umbilicus, lochia appropriate.

Labs: Hgb 12.5 g/dL, WBC 8.0 K, platelets 250 K. TSH 2.5. UA normal.

Impression: acute postpartum psychosis. Infant safe with husband and grandmother at home.
Plan: psychiatry consulted; voluntary admission to inpatient psychiatry accepted. Methadone dose confirmed with program for inpatient continuation.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Inpatient Psychiatry
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PSYCHIATRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY (released with patient consent)
Admission 11/27/2019 - Discharge 12/09/2019

Reason for admission: postpartum psychosis with onset in the first postpartum week - insomnia, auditory hallucinations, delusional belief that her newborn was possessed, disorientation.

Hospital course: Admitted voluntarily. Medical causes considered; ED labs including CBC, TSH and urinalysis were normal. Started olanzapine, titrated to 10 mg at bedtime. Sleep was protected with nursing support. Hallucinations faded over the first week, and by day 8 she was oriented, sleeping 7 hours, and had full insight that her beliefs about the baby had been part of an illness. She denied any thoughts of harming herself or the infant throughout. She pumped regularly on the unit and maintained her milk supply; olanzapine is considered compatible with breastfeeding and she plans to resume nursing at home. Husband and her mother participated in family meetings and will provide overnight infant care for the coming weeks so she can sleep.

Methadone 60 mg daily continued in coordination with her treatment program.

Mental status at discharge: calm, linear, euthymic, no perceptual disturbance, oriented x3, insight and judgment good.

Diagnosis: postpartum psychosis.
Discharge medications: olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime; methadone 60 mg daily (OTP); prenatal vitamin daily; sumatriptan as needed.
Follow-up: outpatient psychiatry 12/17; primary care within one week. Safety plan reviewed with patient and husband.

PCP: thanks. Please book a visit within a week of discharge when we hear.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen with husband and baby (26 days old). Discharged from inpatient psych 12/9 after admission for postpartum psychosis. Discharge summary reviewed.

She says she feels "like myself again, just tired." No voices since about a week into the admission. Understands what happened and is shaken by it. Sleeping 6-7 hrs - husband and her mom take the overnight feeds with pumped milk, she nurses during the day. Taking olanzapine 10 mg at bedtime every night. Methadone 60 mg, dosing at program, no cravings. Bleeding tapering. Breastfeeding going ok.

No thoughts of self-harm or harming the baby. Husband agrees she seems herself.

Exam: tired but bright, appropriate, linear, no evidence of responding to internal stimuli. Abdomen soft, nontender. PHQ-9 = 6 (sleep, energy, appetite items).

A/P
1. Postpartum psychosis, resolving on olanzapine - psychiatry f/u 12/17 confirmed. Keep protected sleep plan. Reviewed warning signs with both of them; they have our cell line and crisis numbers.
2. OUD in sustained remission - stable; program aware of admission.
3. Postpartum - OB visit at 6 weeks (12/30).
4. Weight still above pre-pregnancy, as expected 4 weeks after delivery.
See me in 4-6 weeks, sooner for any concern.

documents.title: Shaky and Heart Racing
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I've felt really shaky and jittery since last weekend and my heart keeps pounding even when I'm sitting. Hard to focus on anything. I'm sleeping when I get the chance but it takes forever to fall asleep. My head feels clear otherwise - no voices or anything like that, I promise I'd tell you. Is this the olanzapine?? My mom says to ask about my thyroid because of my sister.

documents.title: Shaky and Heart Racing
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me right away. Olanzapine doesn't usually do that. Your mom has a good point - thyroid inflammation after delivery is fairly common and causes exactly this. Please come Monday morning for blood work (thyroid and blood count); order is in. If your heart is racing with chest pain, fainting or trouble breathing, go to the ED. I'm also letting your psychiatrist know.

Her watch shows a fast resting heart rate. No chest pain, no syncope. Advised to hold off on extra caffeine. Psychiatry FYI sent; she is still free of psychotic symptoms. She knows to go to the ED for chest pain, fainting or confusion.

ENDOCRINOLOGY CONSULTATION
Patient: Jill Woodward   Seen: 12/30/2019; uptake study 12/31/2019
Requested by: primary care, for suppressed TSH six weeks postpartum

I saw Ms. Woodward this afternoon; she had her obstetric postpartum visit this morning. She delivered a healthy term daughter six weeks ago and is breastfeeding without difficulty. Around two weeks ago she began to feel restless with frequent palpitations and trouble keeping her focus, and her clothes have become looser although she is not trying to lose weight and her appetite is unchanged. No chest pain, dyspnea or recent illness. No anterior neck pain, no change in vision.

Recent history is notable for postpartum psychosis requiring a two-week admission, now on olanzapine and recovering well. Opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg daily. Migraine without aura.
Medications: methadone 60 mg daily, olanzapine 10 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan as needed.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: sister with Hashimoto thyroiditis; mother with hypothyroidism.

Exam: HR 102 and regular. Fine tremor of both outstretched hands. Thyroid slightly enlarged and firm, not tender, no discrete nodule. No lid lag, no proptosis.

Data: TSH 0.02, free T4 2.4 (12/23, drawn by primary care). Radioactive iodine (I-123) uptake 12/31 is low. She pumped and discarded milk for the interval nuclear medicine advised and has resumed nursing.

Impression: thyrotoxicosis with low uptake six weeks after delivery - postpartum thyroiditis, thyrotoxic phase. Low uptake argues against Graves disease. This is a destructive, self-limited process; antithyroid drugs would not help.

Plan:
- Propranolol 10 mg up to three times a day as needed for palpitations and tremor; compatible with breastfeeding.
- Repeat thyroid tests in about six weeks. Many patients pass through a hypothyroid phase in the following months; I will see her again then.
- Copy to obstetrics and psychiatry.

Endocrinology

documents.title: Perinatal Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
PERINATAL PSYCHIATRY CONSULTATION
Patient: Jill Woodward   Date: 2/20/2025
Referred by primary care for preconception planning.

Ms. Woodward is 38 and planning a second pregnancy. In November 2019, ten days after her first delivery, she developed an acute psychosis with insomnia, auditory hallucinations and a delusional belief about her infant, treated with a two-week admission and olanzapine; full remission, medication stopped 10/2020, no episodes since. No mood or psychotic episodes outside the postpartum period. Postpartum thyroiditis in the same period. Opioid use disorder in sustained remission on methadone 60 mg for over ten years. Maternal aunt with bipolar I; mother with postpartum depression.

Mental status today: well-groomed, warm, euthymic, linear, no perceptual disturbance, excellent insight.

Discussion: Her risk of a recurrent postpartum psychosis after the next delivery is substantial - in the range of one in three or higher. Prophylactic lithium started immediately after delivery lowers that risk considerably; it would require level monitoring and planning around breastfeeding. Alternatives are an antipsychotic after delivery, or no medication with intensive monitoring. She and her husband asked good questions. She does not want to take lithium or restart olanzapine, and prefers a non-medication plan with close follow-up, understanding that medication would be started at the first warning sign.

Plan:
- No psychotropic medication in pregnancy or prophylactically after delivery, per her informed choice.
- Protected sleep after delivery: husband and her mother cover night feeds (pumped milk or formula), at least one 6-hour sleep block per night.
- Follow-up visit in the third trimester to finalize the written plan; early postpartum check-ins by video in weeks 1, 2 and 4, plus primary care.
- Warning signs reviewed with both: insomnia beyond one night, confusion, odd beliefs, hearing voices - same-day evaluation.
